goals.title: Dual-source search: local library plus YouTube
goals.description: Design frames 1f, 1g and 1h. One search field querying two sources at once: the indexed local music folders (instant, already available via LibraryIndex in ipod-gui.py) and YouTube via 'yt-dlp ytsearch --flat-playlist --dump-json'. Local results paint immediately; YouTube results arrive 1-3s later into a reserved three-row skeleton so the layout never jumps. Note that youtube_unavailable_reason() is too strict to gate search on its own, because metadata search works without a JavaScript runtime; only the media download 403s. Reuse yt_dlp_bin and yt_dlp_supports from lib.sh. Design all five failure states: no JS runtime, ffmpeg missing, rate-limited or offline, download failed mid-fetch, and no results from either source. Each must be stated inline in place of the section that cannot load, never as a toast.

goals.title: GStreamer preview playback and the live now-playing bar
goals.description: The now-playing bar exists in ipod-gui.py in its idle state only; its transport controls are insensitive. Wire it to GStreamer playbin3 with position polled on a 250ms GLib timeout, per design frame 1n, which specifies all four bar states: idle, fetching, playing a local file, and playing a previewed track. Playback is preview only, on the computer's speakers, and never touches the iPod. Add a gst_available predicate to lib.sh modelled on find_gui_python - a separate function, because extending find_gui_python would make the whole GUI unavailable when GStreamer is missing - and reach it from the GUI through the existing lib_function_succeeds bridge. Adding system dependencies is approved, so this needs no further sign-off. Note python3-gi-cairo is still NOT required: the storage meter uses a CSS gradient rather than Cairo drawing, deliberately, because a missing converter would make the bar silently render as nothing.

goals.title: Preview cache with promote-on-add
goals.description: Previewing a YouTube result downloads it first (about 4s) rather than streaming: yt-dlp -g URLs are short-lived and IP-bound, seeking over HTTP is unreliable, and streaming throws the work away so Add would fetch a second time. Downloads land in a prunable cache, not straight into the library, so previewing twenty songs does not silently add twenty files to the user's music folder. Adding a previewed track promotes it into ~/Music/youtube and out of the cache. This is what finally creates the third track state, STATE_PREVIEW, which ipod-gui.py already defines and renders everywhere (dimmed artwork, dashed marker) but nothing currently produces. Wire up the Preview cache card in Device and Settings, which is present but shows 0 B and has its Clear button disabled.

goals.title: YouTube thumbnails as album art
goals.description: Search results and previewed tracks need artwork. ipod-fetch.sh passes --no-embed-thumbnail explicitly, commented 'Cover art is pure waste on a 2GB device with no screen' - still true for the device, but the desktop grid needs it. Either fetch thumbnails separately into the existing art cache or revisit that flag for previewed tracks only. Load them as GdkTexture through the existing make_cover helper, which already handles a missing-art fallback to a generated striped placeholder.

goals.title: Add GStreamer to install.sh as an optional system dependency
goals.description: Follow the existing capability-probe pattern in install.sh: probe for the capability rather than the package name, print an 'info' line when present, and append apt names to the 'needed' array when absent. GStreamer belongs in 'needed' like ffmpeg, not in the js_runtime exception - that exception exists because Ubuntu ships nodejs 18 below yt-dlp's floor of 22, and GStreamer has no equivalent version hazard. Add a matching line to the Verifying section. PyGObject stays out of the venv for the documented reason, so anything GStreamer-Python is a system dependency too.

goals.title: Split ipod-gui.py into a package and modernise the test harness
goals.description: ipod-gui.py is now a very large single module and wants to be a package. It was deliberately left as one file: the three smoke tests load it via spec_from_file_location with no package context and no sys.modules entry, and they patch module globals late (ipod_gui.find_ipods, ipod_gui.YOUTUBE_LIBRARY). A naive split silently breaks that patching - 'from .detect import find_ipods' rebinds the name and the detection test would pass against unpatched code, which is worse than failing. Do the split together with a test-harness rewrite. Also extend the CI Python gate, currently only 'py_compile ipod-gui.py tests/*.py', which would not cover new files. Keep AUDIO_EXTENSIONS a module-level set of dot-prefixed strings, or re-export it: gui-actions-smoke.py regex-scrapes SUPPORTED_EXT from lib.sh and asserts set equality. Natural seams now that the file has grown: the tag/scan bridge, the Track/Album/LibraryIndex model, the CSS token sheet and shared widget helpers (make_cover, track_column_view, track_list_view, StorageMeter), and the window itself.

goals.title: Move blocking device work in refresh() off the main loop
goals.description:
count_tracks, list_tracks, list_playlists, spoken_playlists and shutil.disk_usage all run synchronously inside IpodWindow.refresh(), over USB. Tag reading and the library scan are already threaded via scan_tracks with a generation counter to discard stale results; extend the same pattern to the rest. This is the largest remaining responsiveness win and it grows with the number of tracks on the device.

Done 2026-08-04. device.py gained probe_device(), which reads detection, identity, saved options, playlists, spoken names, the track count and free space in one pass and returns a DeviceProbe built complete or not at all. refresh() bumps a probe_generation, hands the read to a worker thread and returns; _apply_probe paints what comes back, and drops a result whose generation was superseded or that landed while a script was changing the device. count_tracks takes the same cancelled callback as scan_tracks, so a superseded walk stops competing for the bus. _populate_device_summary and the wipe dialog read the cached figures rather than the device, so a repaint costs nothing.

list_tracks turned out not to be called from window.py at all, so only the other four moved. Two states came out of it that the old code could not express: a device that stops answering mid-read is now reported as that, rather than as a connected iPod holding nothing, and the first paint says it is looking rather than claiming there is no iPod - which matters because findmnt alone waits five seconds on a device that has stopped answering.

goals.title: Search UI polish deferred from the redesign
goals.description:
Small things the phase-1 redesign left, all in ipod-gui.py. The library filter pills count collections but the heading and counts stay collection-shaped while the list mode shows tracks, which reads slightly off. The album detail's state, duration and action cluster sits hard against the right edge with a wide gap after the title column. The playlist rail and the shelf both render the same playlists with different tile sizes. None of these block anything; fold them into whichever phase touches those views next.

Done 2026-08-04. The library heading, its pill counts and what those pills filter now follow the mode: list mode reads Tracks over per-track counts, and filters the tracks themselves, so a synced track is no longer hidden by its album still counting as In library. LibraryIndex gained track_counts() for that, which counts() cannot answer.

The album page is held to TRACK_PAGE_WIDTH in an Adw.Clamp, header and table together. Unclamped it had been the worst case in the app: on a 1900px window the title ended at x=460 and the state, duration and action cluster sat at x=1680. The playlists detail took the same clamp, since its rows are the same rows and it stretches further still.

Playlist artwork is now three named sizes rather than four arbitrary ones: the shelf tile takes ALBUM_COVER so the two sections of the library page use one artwork size, and both rails take PLAYLIST_ROW_COVER so a playlist row looks the same in the sidebar and in the Playlists view. Shelf tiles were also ragged - each sized to its own name - and are now uniform, with the card inset left to the button's own padding so four playlists and the New tile still fit at the opening window size.

Two defects surfaced while looking at these views and were fixed with them: the Playlists rail took a share of every extra pixel of window, because the heading and every row expand and GTK propagates that up, so at 1900px a 240px list held half the view; and the playlist's spoken-name line wrapped at 34 characters however much room it had.

Verified by rendering each view offscreen at 1180 and 1900 and reading the result, since x11grab sees black under Wayland and a WidgetPaintable holds nothing when the compositor is not sending the window frames: forcing the layout with Gtk.Widget.allocate and snapshotting into a Cairo renderer makes the size a parameter of the shot rather than whatever the window manager gave.

goals.title: Let ipod-sync.sh copy symlinked music
goals.description:
ipod-sync.sh:424 enumerates a source with 'find "$src" -type f -print0'. find does not dereference symlinks by default, so a symlinked audio file is -type l and is silently never copied, and a symlinked subdirectory is never descended. Symlinked library layouts are common, so this is a real long-standing limitation rather than a deliberate policy - it just was not visible before, because nothing counted what was about to be copied.

Verified 2026-08-03: for a directory containing a symlink to an mp3, 'find -type f' returns nothing while Python's os.walk plus Path.is_file() counts the file.

The GUI redesign surfaced this as a mismatch (review-23 in the no-mistakes run merged as PR #11) because it counts queued tracks to drive a progress bar: counting a symlinked track the script then skips means the sync exits successfully with progress short of 100 percent. That was resolved by aligning the GUI DOWNWARD to the script - it now skips symlinks too - so the counts are honest. Making the script actually copy them was the better long-term answer.

Work: switch to 'find -L' (or -follow) in the source enumeration, then add e2e coverage for the cases that makes newly reachable - a symlink loop, a broken symlink, a symlinked directory, and a symlink pointing outside the source tree - and decide whether a symlink escaping the selected folder should be copied at all. Remove the GUI-side symlink skip and its user-facing note at the same time, otherwise the two halves disagree again in the opposite direction.

Done 2026-08-04. ipod-sync.sh enumerates a source with 'find -L "$src" \( -type f -o -type l \) -print0', so a symlinked track is copied and a symlinked folder is descended. A link is followed wherever it points, including out of the folder being synced, because that is what a linked layout is for and the link is only ever read: the copy lands where the link sits inside the source and never where it points, so following one cannot write outside the music directory. That is the opposite of ipod-remove.sh, which resolves before checking containment because it deletes.

Under -L, -type l matches only a link that cannot be resolved, so one walk finds the tracks and the broken links together. A broken link named like a track is reported by path and counted; one named like a cover image stays quiet, because it was never going to be copied. find detects a folder that links back into itself, walks it once and reports it on stderr while exiting 1 - that used to arrive as raw find output in the middle of the copy log, and is now captured and repeated in the script's own voice, which covers an unreadable folder the same way.

The GUI side went the other way, as the goal asked: skip_symlinks, the recursive-no-symlinks reader mode, the per-source skipped counts and the 'symlinked item skipped' toasts and queue-label note are gone, and scan_tracks returns (records, complete). The scan follows links to agree with the script, which needed a loop guard of its own: os.walk has no loop detection and would have recursed forever, so each directory carries its ancestry and one that is its own ancestor is dropped. It deliberately does not dedupe more widely, because two links to one folder are two folders to find, which copies both. tags.walk_following_links holds that rule for _audio_files; the reader cannot call it, being source text run by whichever interpreter has mutagen, so the two are kept deliberately alike.

Fixed along the way: a single dangling *.mp3 link anywhere under a music root made the whole library scan exit 2, so the user saw an empty library because of one broken link. Verified before the change - a folder with good.mp3 next to a dangling link returned no records and complete false.

Covered end to end on its own device, since a source holding a filesystem loop is not something to leave in the shared one: a linked track, a linked folder with a subfolder, a link out of the tree, a dangling audio link, a dangling non-audio link that stays quiet, and a parent loop. tests/gui-scan-paths.py prints what the scan finds so the suite can hold it against what the sync copied, which is the mismatch this goal existed to close. Mutation-checked: reverting to 'find -type f' aborts the suite exactly at that scenario, copying 1 of 4 tracks.

goals.title: Break up the 4368-line ipod_gui/window.py
goals.description:
The package split left IpodWindow as one module, deliberately: the goal named 'the window itself' as one seam, and splitting a single Adw.ApplicationWindow subclass across files needs mixins, which was too much to combine with the split and its test-harness rewrite in one change.

It is now by far the largest module - 4368 lines against 457 for the next one, player.py - and it holds every view plus the work behind each. Natural seams inside it: the library grid and album detail, the playlist views and their drag reordering, the search field and its two result sections, the Device & Settings page, and the sync/remove/wipe command plumbing with its busy-state bookkeeping.

Mixin classes are the only split that keeps one Adw.ApplicationWindow, so the question to settle first is whether the shared self.* state between those groups is small enough for mixins to be honest rather than a filing system over one namespace. tests/harness.py makes the mechanics safe: it writes a replacement to every module holding a name, so moving methods between modules cannot silently unpatch a check the way it would have before.

Done 2026-08-05. Split into seven mixins over one Adw.ApplicationWindow: library_view, search_view, playlist_view, playback_view, device_view, queue and commands, with window.py keeping the chrome, the state and the assembly order. The largest module is now device_view.py at 929 lines against 4438 before, in line with device.py at 527 and player.py at 457.

The question the goal asked first was settled by measuring rather than by judgement. Counting __init__ makes every attribute look shared, because it is the one place all of them are born; excluding it, 33 of 152 attributes are touched by more than one module, and two thirds of those by exactly two. What is genuinely window-wide is small: the device the window is pointed at, whether a script is running, and the library and the player. So mixins are honest here - but only after the seams were redrawn. The first cut had device and sync sharing twelve attributes, which said they were one concern wearing two names; commands and queue is the cut that works.

Sixteen shared attributes went away rather than being written down, because they were shared only for being built in one module and painted in another. The sidebar's device card, the header's search field and library controls, the playlist rail and the shelf at the top of the library page now belong to whichever mixin repaints them, and the window appends what they return without naming it. Closing the window reached into playback's lock and process handle and now calls one verb; reading the visible view became current_view() for the same reason, since a verb is a declared interface and a widget reached into is not. window.py is left touching exactly one attribute another mixin owns.

device_view.py stayed the largest deliberately. Splitting its page from its probe was measured too, and makes it worse: 33 shared attributes become 36, with 12 shared between the two halves, because painting a device summary and probing the device are one concern.

tools/mixin-contract.py is what keeps this from rotting back. It pins the shared table and checks it in both directions, so a new sharer fails and an entry the code has left behind fails too - adding to it is allowed, doing it by accident is not. It also catches a method defined in two mixins, an attribute read but never assigned, and state assigned but never read. That last check found three dead attributes: now_playing_bar, settings_view and sync_files, all written and never consulted, now gone.

tests/gui-window-build.py builds the real window under xvfb, which nothing did before. Every other GUI check runs methods unbound against a stand-in, deliberately, so none would notice a builder that stopped being called or a widget that never reached the stack - exactly what a mixin split risks. CI gained xvfb for it.

Every one of the 159 methods moved with an identical AST, checked against the pre-split file, so the move could not reword anything; the 11 call sites that did change are the seven extracted builders and the four dead-attribute removals. Both new checks were mutation-tested - removing a builder call, dropping a view from the stack, reaching into another mixin's state, defining a method twice, and mistyping an attribute each fail the check that should catch them. Writing gui-window-build.py surfaced a defect in itself: an exception escaping a GLib idle callback does not end the main loop, so it hung rather than failed, and it now has a watchdog and its own try/except. Full product-e2e.sh passes, 66 checks.

goals.title: Make it easier to create a new playlist
goals.description:
Currently, in order to create a new playlist, you need to choose a playlist file.

Instead, creating a playlist should be low friction like spotify where it creates everything for you, and you just get the option to name the new playlist (start with default name like Playlist #_ if none is typed). 

Then it should be easy to add songs to the playlist from yt-dlp or from the existing library. It should also be easy to move songs between playlists and remove back to the standard library.

If you have any other suggestions let me know, i'm open to anything.

Done 2026-08-05. A playlist is now a file the app writes rather than one you had to bring with you: one M3U per list under ~/Music/Playlists, which ipod_gui/playlists.py owns. Making one is a name and nothing else - the new dialog offers the next free 'Playlist N', refuses a name FAT cannot hold while it is being typed rather than letting ipod-sync.sh mangle it into a different spoken name two steps later, and writes the file when it closes. No iPod, no export from another program, no sync to wait for.

Songs go in from a ⋯ menu on every track row - the library table, an album page, and both halves of the search results - plus an album-level Add to playlist. A YouTube result carries the same menu: it downloads first and lands in the playlist when it finishes, found by video id rather than by what the run reported, because a video the music folder already holds downloads nothing and reports nothing. A previewed track is kept into the library before it is listed, since an entry pointing into a cache that gets pruned would stop resolving with nothing having been deleted on purpose. Inside a playlist the same menu moves a track to another playlist or removes it, which is what the goal asked for and leaves the song itself alone.

Every edit rewrites the file and stages the playlist and its tracks for the next sync; an emptied one is still staged, because the sync is what removes the device's copy. Editing with no iPod attached is not a failure - Send to iPod stages it when one turns up. Without a speech engine the playlist stays here and the page says why, which is the old refusal moved from making a playlist to putting one on a screenless device.

Device playlists are still listed beside them - a folder or tag grouping, or a list made elsewhere - but read-only, because their entries name scrambled files on the iPod with no local counterpart to write down. The rail and shelf now carry the same state dot a track does, since the spoken-name marker they used to show says nothing about a playlist that has never been synced, and every new one starts out as exactly that. Add playlist file… became Import playlist file…, which adopts the list into the folder with its entries resolved instead of pointing at where it sat.

Two defects were caught by measuring rather than by looking. A row of four action buttons took the narrowest the window could be from 640px to 730px, past the point where the sidebar has already folded away to make room; it is two buttons and a ⋯ now, and the Playlists view is narrower than before this goal at 426→574px against 545px. And a ⋯ at row opacity beside two solid buttons reads as disabled, so the one a page carries alone is full strength.

Covered by tests/gui-playlists.py, which asserts the file after every edit and what each one staged, and by two end-to-end steps that take a list built by that same store through ipod-sync.sh: the order a track was dragged into survives onto the device, and emptying a playlist removes it from the device while keeping its songs. Eleven mutations checked, each caught by the check that should: de-duplication, staging, re-staging the source of a move, deleting the file, removing the old device playlist after a rename, the emptied-playlist rule, refusing a device-only track, the row menu, selecting a new playlist, painting the detail, and queueing the list itself alongside its tracks. Full product-e2e.sh passes, 69 checks.

goals.title: Add top bar to maximize/minimize/close the window
wipe the ipod and redownload everything
add queued filter and symbol on library page
Answer a deleted playlist apart from one that could not be read
goals.description: playlist_contents catches every OSError alike, so a playlist another program deleted while its rows are on screen answers complete=False and the window says it could not write - sending the user to check permissions on a folder that is perfectly writable, while the rail keeps showing a playlist that is gone. Making playlist_contents answer FileNotFoundError apart from a genuine read failure closes it for add_entries, remove_entry and move_entry at once, rather than at each of the three edit sites. A deleted playlist should repaint, the way a vanished row already does; a real read failure should keep saying so. Raised by review on playlist-edit-failure-wording, which fixed the shortened-file half of the same symptom. Deliberate and module-wide today: tests/gui-playlists.py asserts the current answer for add_entries on a deleted file, so those assertions move with the change.

goals.title: Get the grouping drop-down working again on a 2x display
goals.description:
DONE 2026-08-07. Not this app's code and not a GTK bug: mutter refused to place the popup and dismissed it. The refusal is in the journal, 491 times in one boot, bursty and clustered on exactly the sessions where the drop-down was being clicked: 'Buggy client caused popup to be placed outside of parent window'. That message has one source in mutter 46, the rect check closing meta_wayland_xdg_popup_post_apply_state, which calls dismiss_invalid_popup and so sends xdg_popup.popup_done when the popup's buffer rect neither overlaps nor touches its parent's. The check runs on the commit that attaches the popup's first buffer, which is the popup_done arriving about 10ms after the map. It also explains the one asymmetry nothing else did: maximised, the parent covers the screen and a mis-placed popup still lands on it; floating, the parent is a small target and the popup misses.

The mis-placement came from the session's layout mode rather than from the widget. DisplayConfig reported layout-mode 2 (physical) with legacy-ui-scaling-factor 2, so mutter was on the legacy HiDPI path, where scale_placement_rule multiplies every positioner coordinate by the window's monitor scale. get_window_geometry_scale_for_logical_monitor returns 1 instead when meta_backend_is_stage_views_scaled is true, which is exactly when scale-monitor-framebuffer is on.

FIXED by turning on Fractional Scaling for the built-in display in Settings, which sets org.gnome.mutter experimental-features to ['scale-monitor-framebuffer'] and moves the session to layout-mode 1 with legacy-ui-scaling-factor 1. The last refusal was logged at 05:04, the display configuration was applied at 05:06:58, and there have been none since. No code changed and the Gtk.DropDown stays. To re-check at any time: journalctl --user -b | grep -c 'outside of parent window' should stay flat while clicking the control.

COST ACCEPTED, and it does not depend on the external monitor being attached: with stage views scaled, mutter hardcodes the UI scaling factor for X11 clients to 1 (meta-settings.c, update_ui_scaling_factor). Measured, X11 clients are told eDP-1 is 1536x960 at scale 1 with Xft.dpi 96, so XWayland apps draw at 1x and are upscaled on the 2x panel where the legacy path had them drawing at 2x; Wayland clients are told scale 2 and stay sharp. GNOME 46 has no xwayland-native-scaling to avoid that. Both displays are on integer scales, 2.0 and 1.0, so nothing is resampled and the power, speed and sharpness warnings on the Settings toggle do not apply to this configuration. The setting is session-wide and stays on undocked, which is what is wanted, because this is a floating-on-a-2x-display bug rather than a two-monitor one and the laptop alone is still 2x.

CORRECTS the earlier reading of the WAYLAND_DEBUG trace: the reactive positioner and the mid-map wp_fractional_scale change are upstream of the mis-placement, not the dismissal itself. The routes listed before are moot - GTK did not need updating past 4.14.5, the Gtk.MenuButton replacement was not needed, and the layered minimal.py reproduction is not needed to verify this.
